items.stem: Before you press Run the training: in the corpus, king and queen share several sentences, and king and hospital never appear together. What do you expect the map to show at the end?

options.text: King and queen end up close together, and king and hospital end up far apart.
options.feedback: Words that appear in the same sentences are pulled together. Words that never appear together are only pushed apart.

options.text: All the words end up in the same place.
options.feedback: Every sentence pulls its own words together, but all words also push each other apart a little, so the map spreads into groups.

options.text: King and hospital end up close, because both are common words.
options.feedback: Closeness here depends on appearing in the same sentences. How common a word is does not matter.

options.text: The words stay where they started.
options.feedback: Each sentence moves the words in it. After many sentences the positions are very different.

items.try: Press Run the training and read the gauge called Groups apart by.

items.stem: A colleague says someone must have labeled the royalty words in advance, or they could not form a cluster. What does the demo show?

options.text: The only input was fourteen sentences. The clusters come from which words appear together, and no labels were used.
options.feedback: The colors on the map are added afterward to show the groups. The training does not use them.

options.text: The program contains a built-in dictionary of word meanings.
options.feedback: There is no dictionary. The program only moves words according to which sentences they appear in.

options.text: The groups only form because the starting positions were chosen by hand.
options.feedback: The starting positions are random. The groups come from the sentences.

options.text: The clusters form because the words were typed in alphabetical order.
options.feedback: The order of the words in the list has no effect on where they end up.

items.stem: The small demo produces clear clusters, but it cannot reproduce the word arithmetic shown in the next panel. Why?

options.text: The finer structure needs each word to appear in thousands of different contexts, and fourteen sentences cannot provide that.
options.feedback: Real training uses billions of words. A small corpus is enough for clusters and too small for the finer patterns.

options.text: The demo only has two dimensions, and arithmetic needs exactly three.
options.feedback: Real models use hundreds of dimensions, but the main limit here is the amount and variety of text.

options.text: The demo does not push words apart.
options.feedback: All words push apart a little in every step. That is how the groups separate.

options.text: Word arithmetic only works for names of places.
options.feedback: The arithmetic works for many kinds of relationships when there is enough text.
